name: M5Stack Unit Hall magnetic sensor
description: Grove-connector magnet sensor from M5Stack: three A3144E unipolar Hall-effect switches (820 Ohm pull-ups) ANDed by a 74HC08D, all on an HT7533 3.3 V rail, so OUT goes low (push-pull, 0 V) while any switch sees a magnet (south pole on the front or north pole on the back; A3144 operate 70-350 G) and high (about 3.3 V) otherwise; a red LED lights while a magnet is detected. Powered from the 5 V Grove supply. Sold as: M5Stack Unit Hall (SKU U084), 32 x 24 mm unit with HY2.0-4P Grove socket OUT, NC, 5V, GND, magnet included.
eli5: A magnet detector on a Grove cable: bring a magnet close and it pulls its output wire low and lights a red LED.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Magnet output (Grove pin 1, white wire): 74HC08 push-pull from 3.3 V, 0 V while a magnet is detected, about 3.3 V otherwise. Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs, no pull-up needed.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply (Grove pin 3, red wire): 5 V into the HT7533 3.3 V regulator.

buildNotes: Grove connector order (M5Stack schematic J1): pin 1 OUT (white), pin 2 NC (yellow), pin 3 5V (red), pin 4 GND (black). The unit has a HY2.0-4P Grove socket, not header pins: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.
Power it from 5 V (ESP32 5V/VIN, Pico VBUS). The on-board HT7533 makes 3.3 V for the Hall switches and the 74HC08, so OUT is at most about 3.3 V and connects straight to a GPIO.
OUT is active low: 0 while a magnet is detected (red LED on), 1 otherwise. It is push-pull, so no pull-up is needed.
Unipolar: the south pole switches it from the front, the north pole from the back.
On an M5Stack Core use Port B (white wire = GPIO36).

driver.code:
# M5Stack Unit Hall (U084), MicroPython driver.
# Schematic (M5Stack): three Allegro-type A3144E unipolar Hall switches U1-U3, each with an
# 820 Ohm pull-up to the unit's 3.3 V rail (HT7533 LDO fed from the Grove 5 V). Their outputs
# A, B, C go into a 74HC08D AND gate (also on 3.3 V): OUT = A AND B AND C, push-pull.
#   A3144E: open-collector output turns ON (pulls low) when B > BOP (south pole facing the
#   branded face, 70-350 G at 25 C) and releases when B < BRP (~55 G hysteresis).
#   So OUT (Grove white wire) is LOW while ANY of the three switches sees a magnet,
#   HIGH (about 3.3 V) otherwise. The red LED (1 kOhm from 3.3 V to OUT) lights while OUT is low.
# OUT is driven by the 74HC08 at 3.3 V: safe for 3.3 V GPIOs, no pull-up needed.
from machine import Pin


class M5Hall:
    def __init__(self, out_pin):
        self.pin = Pin(out_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(out_pin, int) else out_pin

    def value(self):
        """Raw level on OUT: 0 = magnet detected, 1 = no magnet."""
        return self.pin.value()

    def magnet(self):
        """True while a magnet is detected (OUT is active low)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 0

    def on_change(self, handler):
        """Call handler(magnet: bool) on every edge of OUT. Pass None to stop."""
        if handler is None:
            self.pin.irq(handler=None)
            return
        self.pin.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING,
                     handler=lambda p: handler(p.value() == 0))

example.code:
from m5_hall import M5Hall
import time

hall = M5Hall({OUT})  # OUT is active low: 0 = magnet
while True:
    print('MAGNET=%d' % hall.magnet())
    time.sleep(0.2)
